identity.title: Central GPU ownership, memory accountability and native lifecycle integration

closure_unit.outcome: Existing and future modules consume one authoritative shared GPU ownership/broker contract with accountable memory/lifecycle and focused typed clients, integrated without replacing adequate canonical components.

materialized_acceptance.text: AC203-1: Ground actual existing canonical GPU ownership/resource-broker mechanics and focused typed clients for existing and future modules. Record authoritative owner, allocation/client identities, dependencies, exact files and source-versus-host contracts before implementation. Reuse adequate capability; no invented mandatory framework, new monolith or assumption of one adapter/API.

AC203-2: All affected modules use centralized authoritative GPU device/queue/resource/pool/budget ownership through scoped typed clients. No per-module independent device/pool/budget bypass; unrelated CPU/NPU work stays in its owning contracts. Prove client/module attachment, detach and multiwindow ownership and denial/isolation conditions.

AC203-3: Bind accountable allocations/reservations/budgets, pressure/admission, staging and shared-versus-dedicated memory attribution to real authoritative resource state. Prove focused positive/negative pressure/budget behavior and truthful diagnostics without arbitrary new caps or fabricated memory success.

AC203-4: Bind submitted/in-flight work settlement, cancellation/retirement and reclamation. Prove resources are not freed before settlement, reclaimed twice or retained beyond owning lifecycle, using actual owned mechanisms and focused lifecycle/pressure checks. Preserve valid partial results and original process/resource protections.

AC203-5: Prove shutdown, device-loss/recovery, window resize/recreation and module attachment/detachment against actual owning typed contracts. Prevent stale clients or leaked ownership after recovery; unsupported cases remain explicit and cannot be hidden by renderer fallback.

AC203-6: Integrate the actual Vulkan GUI as a client of that owner with genuine backend/device/memory/lifecycle evidence on exact native inputs. D3D/OpenGL fallback is not Vulkan. Reusable canonical gaps need separate proven published source before host adoption; exact unchanged proof is reused. Current runtime/fetch/physical custody and scoped human retry authority remain, no automatic execution grant.

AC203-7: Actual allocation/pressure/staging/in-flight settlement/reclaim/shutdown/device-loss/recovery/window/module lifetime failures are observable through internal_diagnostics and correlated standalone Palmistry records with mechanical typed metadata/privacy. Reuse canonical watcher and allowlist; the broker/GUI does not become a copied watcher, recovery executor or OS remediation controller.

rf_12_mapping.attach: ClaimRequest module and client; GpuOwner::revoke_client is the detach that stops submissions and keeps charges
rf_12_mapping.reserve: GpuOwner::admit: bytes, bounded by limit_bytes, max_claims and max_in_flight_per_claim of the host policy
rf_12_mapping.submit: GpuOwner::submit: the client records into the owner's command buffer, the owner alone touches the queue
rf_12_mapping.observe: GpuOwner::observe (no wait) and GpuOwner::wait (bounded); the owner reads its own timeline semaphore, a client never reports completion
rf_12_mapping.carried_by_submission: module, client, operation, operation id, device generation and fence value (timeline value)

gpu_contract_result.allocation_and_memory_model: Quota admission and per-claim reservation with committed and staging charges inside it; retained memory stays charged under its lease until released; unmeasured never becomes zero; a settlement that reports less than the claim has charged is refused; driver heap estimates are a separate view and are never merged. Allocation itself is the client's in this slice (G203-H1).
gpu_contract_result.inflight_and_reclamation: One timeline semaphore per generation. A submission is counted before the queue takes it and ends only when the owner observes its value, the loss of a quiescent device, the destruction of its device, or that it never reached the queue. Settlement and rebind are refused while anything is in flight; command pools are freed only after their value passed.
gpu_contract_result.shutdown_loss_recovery_windows_modules: Only VK_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST is loss. A lost device is destroyed only when no lease, recording or wait holds it and it is quiescent; otherwise the rebind is refused with a typed reason. Rebind keeps the adapter, generation + 1, charge moved once, nothing refunded. Close drains, destroys or truthfully retains. Windows and detachment beyond revocation are not in this slice.

source_adoption_binding.reason: No asset source or dependency is linked. The port and the UI pass are adopted by a later distinct pinned change once the asset publishes a wgpu-free port and takes an injected device (HBR-MODULE-LIFECYCLE-004/007/008).

gaps.gap: Device injection: the Studio Vulkan renderer does not take a host device. Owner::open_device calls create_device itself; Core, the only holder of device and queue, is pub(crate) and destroys both in Drop; UiPass::new/with_limits take &Owner and clone its private Core; UiPass::draw takes &mut Owner and a PaneId. DeviceLease (raw handles) has a producer and no consumer. The crate documentation says 'takes a host-supplied device (O4)'; no entry point does.
gaps.host_side_ready: GpuOwner::lease returns DeviceHandles with the fields of that DeviceLease plus features, and keeps the device alive until the lease is dropped.
gaps.still_differs: The asset DeviceLease has generation u32 (host u64), issuer only TransientAssetLocal, and no features field although UiPass requires dynamicRendering.

gaps.gap: Asynchronous settlement: every upload and every UI pass ends in Submitter::submit_wait, which submits to the queue itself and waits up to FENCE_TIMEOUT_NS on a fence; per-pass buffers are reused on the assumption that the wait returned. A host that owns the queue and observes completion later needs recording separated from submission and per-submission resources.
gaps.host_side_ready: GpuOwner::submit hands the client the owner's command buffer to record into, returns a Submission at once, and the owner observes its timeline value (observe without waiting, wait with a bound).

gaps.gap: The canonical port is not linkable without wgpu: GpuClientPort, GpuGrant and GrantLedger live in hsk-studio-render-gpu, which depends on wgpu =27.0.1 unconditionally. Linking it would put wgpu into this unit's closure (D7).
gaps.host_side_ready: The unit's records carry the port's admission and settlement fields without loss (module u32, client u64, operation, requested bytes; retained, peak, evictions, native_driver, in_flight, outcome including abandoned). The port's DeviceRef selects among devices; here the one bound device is meant and an adapter assigns its u64.

gaps.gap: A host grant cannot carry a device or the owner's generation: GpuGrant's lease is a crate-private wgpu DeviceLease; issue_host and rebind_host pass lease None and fix generation 1 or old + 1; the backend turns such a grant into Unavailable(no_device).

Port outcomes the owner needs and the port lacks: no release of retained memory after a settlement that reports retained bytes (the owner keeps it charged until release_retained); no refusal for work in flight or a held device on rebind, for the claim and in-flight bounds, for a held lease at settlement, or for retained numbers that contradict the claim's charges; AdmissionRequest has no operation id and no authorization provenance (GPU-QUOTA-008/010), GpuOperation has no render.

gaps.owner: renderer asset, capability question for the packet lead
gaps.gap: hsk-studio-render-gpu-native-memory (handpick) already reads VK_EXT_memory_budget but only from a wgpu device, so a pure-Vulkan owner cannot consume it. GpuOwner::memory_snapshot reads the same properties from the owner's own device. If the asset publishes a raw-handle observer, this unit should consume it (HBR-COMPONENT-001).

No owner-side allocation and no owner images: clients allocate from a lease and report charges. The render attachment of an injected pass (image, view, format, extent, layouts) is therefore not typed here. RF-12 does not define the word attachment; here it is the module and client attribution a submission carries.
The instance enables no surface extension, the device no swapchain, and submit takes no wait or signal semaphores, so nothing can present yet.

Not here: kernel issuer and grants (NATIVE-RENDER-BOOT-002/007, GPU-QUOTA-011), installation-wide persisted quota ledger (GPU-QUOTA-006..010), forwarding OwnerDiagnostics into internal_diagnostics and Palmistry (AC203-7), an owner-side settlement for a claim whose handle was dropped.

Nothing has run. A real device loss has not been provoked; the loss path is covered by pure tests and, for submit and observe, by a device test that skips with a typed reason when no acceptable Vulkan device exists.

outcome is never read: after DeviceLost, Completed or NoEffect still gets a receipt (GUI-DESKTOP-033, GPU-QUOTA-014)
probe waits idle, unbounded, under slot and queue locks
one unreturned lease blocks recovery for all; idle lease holders are not told of a loss
a dropped Claim leaks bytes and a slot until process exit; dropped Submissions clear only through blocking calls
no opaque module, client or claim ids, so attribution cannot survive (GUI-DESKTOP-029/050); a retained device's later destruction or leak is not reported
shared versus dedicated not attributable on integrated GPUs; close may report retained with 0 holders; in-flight bound checked after recording; ash::Entry::load uses default DLL search
